kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea YELLOW/ADVISORY - The Halema'uma'u eruption of Kīlauea is paused following episode 57 fountaining on the morning of November 23. Summit inflation immediately restarted indicating that another episode is likely in the coming weeks.
kilauea_notices.detail: Overview: Episode 57 lava fountaining began from the north vent from 12:15 a.m. and paused at 6:00 a.m. HST on November 23, 2026. Last night both the north and southwest vent showed moderate to weak glow and strong degassing since the end of episode 57. All summit tiltmeters show inflation resuming after episode 57 ended, indicating that another episode is likely in the coming weeks. A new forecast window will be provided in the coming days once enough tilt data has been collected for an accurate forecast. Details and a chronology of episode 57 are included in a status report here: https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-HVO-2026-11-23T17:33:15+00:00 Summit Observations: Summit webcams recorded moderate to weak, nearly continuous, glow from both the north and southwest vents overnight. Incandescent areas are still visible at night within the lava flow emplaced during episode 57 and they may persist for several days as the lava flow cools. Since the end of episode 57 at 6:00 a.m. HST on November 23, tilt at UWD has inflated by approximately 4.4 microradians after losing approximately 18 microradians during episode 57. Other summit tiltmeters also show a change from deflation to inflation following the end of episode 57. Seismicity followed the normal pattern by returning to low-level tremor with bursts every 5-10 minutes following the end of episode 57, which has continued over the past day. Five earthquakes were located within the summit region over the past day. The summit vents are emitting a robust plume of volcanic gases. Winds remain out of the north to northeast, blowing the gas plume to the southwest. The gas array measured approximately 5500 t/d of SO2 yesterday (November 23, 2026). Rift Zone Observations: Rates of seismicity and ground deformation remain low in the East Rift Zone and Southwest Rift Zone. SO2 emissions from the East Rift Zone remain below the detection limit. Analysis: Following the end of episode 57 on November 23, 2026, summit tiltmeters have recorded a typical post-fountaining recovery, with continuous inflationary tilt at UWD. The abrupt switch from summit deflation to inflation at the end of episode 57, continued glow from the vents, and the resumption of low frequency tremor bursts indicate that another lava fountaining episode is likely in the coming weeks. It is too early to forecast when any future episode might occur. Kīlauea has been erupting episodically since December 23, 2024, from two primary vents (north and south) within Halemaʻumaʻu at the summit. Lava fountaining episodes generally last less than 12 hours and are separated by pauses of two or more weeks. HVO continues to closely monitor Kīlauea and remains in contact with Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park and the Hawaiʻi County Civil Defense Agency regarding eruptive hazards. Summary of episode 57 (Episode 57 Status Report): Lava fountaining occurred between 12:15 a.m. and 6:00 a.m. on November 23, 2026. Maximum fountain heights were about 660 feet (200 meters). Only the north vent produced fountaining. Tephra fallout was primarily towards the southwest, in closed areas of Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park. The eruptive plume rose as high as 20,000 feet (6,000 meters) above sea level. Tiltmeter data indicate just under 8 million cubic yards (6 million cubic meters) of lava erupted, with an average eruption rate of 275 cubic yards (210 cubic meters) per second. The Uēkahuna tiltmeter (UWD) recorded a total of 18 microradians of deflationary tilt. Hazards: Eruptive activity since December 2024 has been occurring within a closed area of Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park. However, recent intrusions highlight that the location of eruptive activity could change. Intrusions can also be hazardous with potential to cause earthquakes, ground cracks, and small landslides. mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts were within typical levels in October, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a slight increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 66 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the October reporting period, after 53 in September. These variations are within the typical range for the past two years. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
